question: How does Qnami differ from direct competitors currently? Summarise it in max 300 words.
answer:
Here’s a concise comparison (under 300 words) of how Qnami differentiates itself from its direct competitors in the quantum sensing space:

Qnami specializes in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center–based quantum sensing using diamond probes, offering high-resolution, nanoscale magnetic field imaging via its flagship ProteusQ scanning NV magnetometer. Launched in 2020, ProteusQ is the first commercial scanning NV magnetometer and is deployed in over ten research institutions across Europe and North America ([quantumzeitgeist.com](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/qnami-partners-with-quantum-design-to-expand-quantum-sensing-technology-to-east-asia/?utm_source=openai)).

Key differentiators include:
• Proprietary Quantilever™ diamond scanning probes, enabling high stability, low drift, and ease of use, praised by users for outperforming custom-built NV setups ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/?utm_source=openai)).  
• A complete system offering: Qnami provides not just hardware but also nano-fabricated diamond chips, integrated systems, and analytics software tailored for nanotechnology, life sciences, and earth sciences ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/?utm_source=openai)).  
• Strategic global distribution: Qnami has partnered with Quantum Design in Japan and Korea to expand its market reach in East Asia ([quantumzeitgeist.com](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/qnami-partners-with-quantum-design-to-expand-quantum-sensing-technology-to-east-asia/?utm_source=openai)).

In contrast, competitors such as QZabre, QuantumDiamonds, AdamantQ, Diatope, SB Quantum, and Nomad Atomics also operate in diamond-based or quantum sensing domains but differ in focus:
• QZabre offers NV magnetometry tools but lacks the integrated microscope system that Qnami provides ([cbinsights.com](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/qnami?utm_source=openai)).  
• QuantumDiamonds emphasizes biocompatible, calibration-free sensors and super-resolution imaging for sectors like biotech and semiconductors ([cbinsights.com](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/qnami?utm_source=openai)).  
• AdamantQ targets timing and sensing components for integration into broader systems ([cbinsights.com](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/qnami?utm_source=openai)).  
• Diatope focuses on engineered diamonds for quantum technologies, including nano‑NMR and quantum computing applications ([cbinsights.com](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/qnami?utm_source=openai)).  
• SB Quantum and Nomad Atomics serve niche markets such as navigation, defense, and gravimetry with specialized sensor types ([cbinsights.com](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/qnami?utm_source=openai)).

In summary, Qnami stands out through its fully integrated, user-friendly NV‑based quantum microscope system, strong academic and industrial adoption, and strategic global partnerships—setting it apart from competitors that offer more component-level or niche quantum sensing solutions.
